title: Social Circuits behind Multi-agent Echo Chambers
summary: Receiver-state interventions trace how messages correct errors or reinforce them, guiding selective communication between agents.
explanation: Agents can agree because evidence corrects a shared mistake, or because repeated claims reinforce it. This example contrasts these two outcomes. Social Circuits traces message effects through receiver activations, and Circuit-Guided Deliberation learns which message combinations help the receiver.
figureCaption: Figure 1 · Error correction and echo chambers

title: CORTEX: Learning to Share and Specialize in Dense Language Models
summary: Domain-conditioned learning dynamics shape shared and specialized functions within a single dense language model.
explanation: CORTEX uses domain-conditioned gradients and cross-domain gradient similarity to identify which parameters support shared or specialized functions. These assignments evolve during training, allowing functional modularity to emerge within one dense model.
figureCaption: Figure 1(b) · Learning shared and specialized functions with CORTEX

title: FLoRG: Federated Fine-tuning with Low-rank Gram Matrices and Procrustes Alignment
summary: Gram-matrix aggregation and Procrustes alignment make federated fine-tuning more consistent and communication-efficient.
explanation: Clients fine-tune a single low-rank matrix, and the server aggregates its Gram matrix to avoid the aggregation error introduced by separately averaging LoRA factors. Procrustes alignment stabilizes the recovered factor between rounds, reducing decomposition drift.

title: ZorBA: Zeroth-order Federated Fine-tuning of LLMs with Heterogeneous Block Activation
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Communications (INFOCOM)
summary: Selective transformer-block activation reduces memory use in gradient-free federated fine-tuning.
explanation: ZorBA assigns different transformer blocks to clients according to their resources and uses forward-pass-only zeroth-order updates. Clients exchange shared random seeds and finite differences instead of full model updates, reducing communication overhead.

title: ASFL: An Adaptive Model Splitting and Resource Allocation Framework for Split Federated Learning
summary: Adapting where a model is split balances learning progress, training delay, and energy consumption.
explanation: ASFL divides model training between resource-constrained clients and a central server. An online optimization algorithm jointly adapts the model split and resource allocation to improve convergence under long-term delay and energy constraints.

title: Tackling Resource Allocation for Decentralized Federated Learning: A GNN-based Approach
summary: A graph neural network coordinates neighbor selection and resource allocation for decentralized learning.
explanation: The model combines a client encoder for node and edge features with a local model encoder for compressed model parameters. A neighbor-selection module chooses aggregation partners, while a decoder outputs resource-allocation decisions for each client.
figureCaption: Figure 3 · The proposed GNN model for decentralized federated learning

title: GNN-based Neighbor Selection and Resource Allocation for Decentralized Federated Learning
summary: Learning which neighbors to aggregate with, and how to allocate resources, in a changing wireless network.
explanation: The framework encodes model parameters, client features, and wireless links with a graph neural network. Neighbor-selection and resource-allocation modules then coordinate decentralized model aggregation and local training.
figureCaption: Figure 2 · Graph-based neighbor selection and resource allocation
